title: Toward High-Accuracy, Programmable Extreme-Edge Intelligence for Neuromorphic Vision Sensors utilizing Magnetic Domain Wall Motion-based MTJ
problem: Edge vision processing suffers from excessive energy consumption for data collection and computation. Neuromorphic vision sensors require energy-efficient, programmable in-pixel processing to reduce backend processing burden on resource-constrained devices.
motivation: Neuromorphic vision sensing with efficient in-pixel processing enables practical deployment of computer vision applications on extreme-edge devices with minimal power consumption.
method: The work proposes a hybrid CMOS+X approach integrating magnetic domain wall magnetic tunnel junctions (MDWMTJ) with CMOS-based neuromorphic pixels to perform in-situ analog convolution. MDWMTJ devices leverage non-volatility and programmability for massively parallel asynchronous computations directly on the sensor. A device-circuit-algorithm co-design framework captures device constraints (low tunnel-magnetoresistance, low dynamic range), circuit constraints (non-linearity, process variation), and algorithm requirements through Monte Carlo simulations with GF22nm FD-SOI technology.
key_novelty: First application of magnetic domain wall motion-based MTJ devices in neuromorphic vision sensors for programmable in-pixel analog convolution.
contributions: First integration of MDWMTJ with neuromorphic vision sensors for in-pixel analog processing
Device-circuit-algorithm co-design framework capturing device and circuit constraints via Monte Carlo simulations
45.3% average reduction in backend-processor energy consumption
High accuracy on DVS-CIFAR10 (79.17%) and IBM DVS128-Gesture (95.99%) datasets
limitations: Device limitations (low tunnel-magnetoresistance, low dynamic range) and circuit constraints (non-linearity, process variation) are analyzed, but practical deployment scalability and comparison with diverse baseline architectures are not extensively discussed.
primary_theme: Energy-efficient neuromorphic vision via magnetic memory devices
